question: None shared. P-62's recorded 0.805-0.920 are balanced accuracies for healthy volunteers vs overt dementia (AD+DLB+iNPH) at two external hospitals; P-62's only MCI result is pathology subtyping within MCI (AD vs DLB vs iNPH, bACC 0.715). P-83 reports MCI vs healthy controls. P-62 never studies MCI vs healthy, and P-83 never studies dementia vs healthy.
metric: Mismatch: balanced accuracy on a dementia vs healthy (or within-MCI subtyping) contrast against segment-level accuracy on MCI vs HC.

figures.P-62: Healthy vs dementia: bACC 0.927 internal (Hospital O, 69 HV/188 patients), 0.805 at Hospital K (n=73) and 0.920 at Hospital N (n=139) external. Within-MCI pathology subtyping at Hospital O (n=83): bACC 0.715, ROC AUC 0.847. No healthy vs MCI figure in the article.
figures.P-83: MCI vs HC, EEG+HRV during CERAD tasks, 15 participants, shuffled 75/25 split of signal segments: average accuracy across tests 93.86%; best test (T1, verbal fluency) 97.43%, AUC 94.91%; T1 10-fold 95.23%, LOOCV 96.14%. The evaluation unit is segments from 15 people, so no subject-level interval can be derived; none is needed because no shared quantity exists.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure: neither paper reports the other's contrast (P-62 has no healthy vs MCI classification; P-83 has no dementia group).
performance_validity: Fails for P-83: its best reported result is 97.43% accuracy (LOOCV 96.14%) on internal validation with n=15 and no external cohort, which meets the Section 3.5 exclusion; the registry's 93.86% is the cross-test average of the same internal segment-level evaluation. P-62's figures pass.
reason: The record labels P-62's healthy vs dementia balanced accuracies as MCI detection; P-62 reports no MCI vs healthy result, so the two papers do not address the same clinical question. The metrics also differ (balanced accuracy vs segment-level accuracy). P-83 separately meets the near-ceiling small-sample exclusion.

quotes.quote: The model demonstrated robustness across institutions, maintaining bACCs of 0.805 for data from Hospital #2 (n = 73) and 0.920 at Hospital #3 (n = 139).
Notably, it also identified MCI pathologies with a bACC of 0.715 for Hospital #1 (n = 83), despite being trained on overt dementia cases instead of MCI cases.
MCI was operationally defined as having a CDR value of 0.5 and an MMSE score of 24 or higher.
Our dataset includes 15 subjects who were randomly assigned to training and testing groups of 7 HC and 8 MCI
